subject: Leadership recap — Orbitra Health decision drivers & procurement checkpoints
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@orbitrahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-10T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Leadership recap — Orbitra Health decision drivers & procurement checkpoints

Aisha / Team —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Below is a concise leadership-level recap so your execs and procurement partners have a single place to review what we covered and what we recommend for next steps. If you want us to reformat into a one-pager for your CFO / procurement, happy to do that.

Key pain & goals (as discussed)
- Current inference costs and latency variability for clinical-document ingestion are driving delays in clinician workflow (~10–15s for long reports).
- Data residency + audit trail are gating any live PHI processing; pilot must run inside your VPC or via our private deployment.
- Need predictable unit economics for regulatory budget sign-off (CFO wants a 12-month run-rate estimate).

Desired business outcomes
- Reduce average inference latency for clinical notes to <2s p50 for short prompts, <20s worst-case for full-doc pipelines.
- Achieve 60–70% cost reduction vs current cloud-attached GPU pipelining through batching, caching, and small-quantized variants for non-clinical steps.
- Operational SLOs: 99.9% uptime during business hours; audit logs for every request.

Risks and mitigation (summary)
- Security/compliance risk: must provide SOC 2 evidence + KMS integration — we will provision SOC artifacts and a KMS checklist (attached: orbitra_risk_rundown_20260410.pdf).
- Procurement timeline risk: procurement needs an SOW and pricing anchor to route for approvals. Draft SOW attached (SOW-draft-orbitra-v1.docx).
- Runway risk: pilot capacity should be reserveable as a dedicated pool with burst to hosted for spike protection.

Proposed procurement path & decision checkpoints
1) Pilot SOW & scope sign-off (2–4 weeks) — objective: run 4-week pilot in VPC with synthetic traffic + 2 pilot customers.
2) Security attestation + audit package delivered (during pilot).
3) Post-pilot exec review: ROI and sizing to confirm committed Dedicated reservation or Private deployment.

Immediate asks / next steps (action owners)
- Aisha / procurement: confirm pilot procurement window and whether Orbitra legal prefers a PO or signed SOW to start. (Aisha)
- Redwood: provide SOC 2 snapshot, KMS integration checklist, and a pricing anchor for pilot (Priyom — see attachments).
- Redwood: update SOW to include canary fallback to hosted API and explicit data-residency text (Marissa / Ben).

Attachments: orbitra_risk_rundown_20260410.pdf, SOW-draft-orbitra-v1.docx

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a clean one-pager for your execs unless you’d prefer the SOW be the single doc.

Best,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
pri...@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@orbitrahealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orbitrahealth.com, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-10T17:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Leadership recap — Orbitra Health decision drivers & procurement checkpoints

Thanks, Priyom — useful summary and appreciated the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Procurement route: procurement@orbitrahealth.com typically needs a signed SOW to begin attaching a PO. We can accept a narrowly-scoped SOW for the pilot, then roll to a master agreement for production.
- Security asks: SOC 2 Type II report or snapshot is sufficient for our initial risk team review. We will flag KMS integrations during the security review, but that is usually an integration step post-SOW.
- Timeline: target to present to our exec committee in 3 weeks (May 1). That means we need final pilot SOW and pricing anchor by April 20 to make the May 1 exec packet.

Can you confirm:
1) whether the pilot estimate includes any per-seat fees for clinical reviewers or strictly inference units?
2) a high-level price band for 3-month committed vs month-to-month pilot (ballpark).

If you can get the SOC snapshot and the pricing anchor into our folder by EOD April 15, we’ll slot you for the April 20 procurement review.

—Aisha
VP, Clinical Operations
Orbitra Health

Marissa / Ben — looping you both to confirm internal owners and timing given Aisha’s procurement window. Key asks from Aisha: final pilot SOW + pricing anchor by 2026-04-20 and SOC 2 snapshot + KMS checklist by 2026-04-15.

Proposal for internal split:
- Marissa: lead SOW update and incorporate the canary-hosted fallback language + explicit data-residency clause. Target draft to me by 2026-04-14 for review.
- Ben: lead pricing anchor — provide two bands (3-month pilot month-to-month pilot pricing, and a 3-month committed discount band). Include assumptions (QPS, avg prompt length, caching %).
- Priyom (me): pull SOC 2 snapshot from security (I’ll request the package now) and assemble KMS integration checklist. I’ll also prepare the one-pager exec summary for Orbitra’s May 1 committee.

Also note: procurement may ask for a short-term credit or pilot discount to lower pilot friction — if you see that as reasonable, propose a pilot concession band in the pricing doc.

Will sync tomorrow EOD on status.

Thanks,
Priyom
